correctness.rationale: Theorem A of Takahasi–Yamamoto is the coding input; the counted objects are unrestricted finite blocks in the closed Dyck coding, not realized or periodic trajectories. Independently, a nonzero-reduction word decomposes uniquely at its unmatched brackets: all unmatched closers precede all unmatched openers, and the gaps are balanced typed Dyck words. A matched pair cannot straddle an unmatched bracket. With C=1+Mt²C² for one balanced gap, summing all numbers of unmatched closers and openers gives C/(1−MtC)². For q=tC this is the claimed OGF, using (1−q)(1−Mq)=(1+Mq²)(1−(M+1)t). For a check of the pole calculation put z=(M+1)t and r=Mq; then z=(M+1)r/(M+r²) and (1−z)²F=(M−r)²/[M(M+r²)]. At z=1 the analytic branch has r=1 and dr/dz=(M+1)/(M−1); the value and negative z-derivative of (1−z)²F there are (M−1)²/[M(M+1)] and 4/(M+1). The double-pole coefficients thus give the stated slope and constant (M+1)/M. The radical is holomorphic in |z|<(M+1)/(2sqrt(M)); r=1 forces z=1, with no other poles. Subtracting the principal part and taking a Cauchy radius 1/ϑ gives exactly the normalized remainder for fixed M≥2. Lagrange extraction gives A_{n,M}=(n+1)^{-1}∑_{k≡n mod 2, 0≤k≤n}(k+1)² M^((n+k)/2) binom(n+1,(n−k)/2); an independent integer evaluation for M=2 and n=0,…,9 matches the table. The entropy refinement follows by expanding the logarithm for large n, not at n=0. The frozen verifiers were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: As a mathematical theorem, exact word complexity for this canonical nonsofic coding is a useful invariant. The linear factor and constant reveal finite-length behavior invisible to the known exponential entropy, across every M≥2 and all interior geometric parameters. The mathematical significance of that theorem is separate from its equivalent coverage in a distinct record; the dimension-three restatement and the entropy expansion are not separate advances.
